newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coles shares rise on profit re-rating.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coles shares rise on profit re-rating.

text.p: Shares in once-struggling retailer Coles Myer Ltd reached a new 12-month high of $5.50 on Wednesday as investors and analysts took heart from the strong performance of rival Woolworths Ltd in the 1996/97 first half.

Coles Myer, which has lagged behind Woolworths in recent years in terms of both sales growth and overall profitability, was 15 cents higher at A$5.45 at 4.00 p.m. (0500 GMT). It was one of the most actively sought stocks, with 2.53 million shares traded.

"Pretty much everything Woolies is saying is positive for Coles Myer, as well in terms of sales having picked up a little bit and margins consolidating," said one Sydney based analyst who asked not to be identified.

"You won't get the improvement to the level of margins that (Woolworths') Big W saw by any means but I think it is generally accepted that there will be some improvement evident at the interim," the analyst said.
Coles Myer was likely to release its 1996/97 first half profit result in mid-March, a company spokeswoman said.
Analysts said the recent appointment of Dennis Eck as chief executive in place of Peter Bartels had also encouraged investors to take another positive look at the retailer.
However, they were divided on the issue of whether or not local institutions were again buying Coles shares in any significant quantities.

The large local investors started dumping their Coles Myer share about two years ago when the company was embroiled in a dispute with the investors about board representation and internal financial and trading procedures.
U.S. fund manager Templeton revealed on Tuesday that it had become a substantial shareholder in the company with a stake of 5.5 percent.
An industry analyst based in Melbourne agreed that the 8.6 percent net profit rise posted by Woolworths on Monday was now helping to underpin the strength in Coles Myer's share price.
"It (the share rise) is just on the back of the Woolworths better-than-expected result," said the analyst, who also asked not to be identified.
"People are inferring that Coles will also surprise on the upside, particularly for the Kmart division."
